name: Soccer Sport Profile
authority: Christian, owner ruling of 6 October 2026. Authorized after the bounded carrier sweep established that the ball is the only sport-level carrier any currently selected game rule requires.
ownershipRule: Sport Profile does not contribute everything that is true of soccer. It contributes constitutive sport structure when the selected game rules require that structure and no existing authoritative source supplies it. — Christian, 6 October 2026.
intendedOwnerEvidence: game-archetype-workbook.rc1.1.json Sport_Profile_Rule: "Detailed sport-specific logic is excluded and must inherit through separate Sport Profile resources." The owner named this layer before it existed; this is its first contribution.
whyItIsNotSelected: A Sport Profile is constitutive rather than selected: it is the environment every activity of this sport operates in, so it reaches every derivation rather than being chosen per goal. It enters through the ordinary contribution-contract pathway (SD-17's shape: a source outside the representation that needs a structural property inside it enters as an item under its own contract, with no separate route), and it carries no new mechanism.
boundaryObserved: The Game Representation contains what a coach lays out and what the rules key on. It represents the rules governing game state, not the evolving state of the game itself. — Christian, 6 October 2026. Accordingly this profile establishes that the ball EXISTS and that the possession relationship is a valid team-valued relationship over the participating opposing teams. It establishes neither the ball's live position nor the current holder of possession; both are game state.
deliberatelyNotContributed: Ordinary Laws of the Game are not authored here: no law becomes an item or a line of the game. RESTATED 23 October 2026 (H2, the d26 design's build step 2) with his authority, his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10: "The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification." The profile now NAMES the Laws as the default (defaultLaws, below) and lists the few that can fail to apply in a modified environment, each with what it needs; an activity's realization records its own departures. Out-of-play triggers still reach a resolved game from the session envelope, and the corpus declines to author them citing by-construction; nothing is blocked on them. Until this restatement the entry read: "Ordinary Laws of the Game: out-of-play behaviour, restarts, offside, legal actions."
Field dimensions and player counts, which the session envelope owns (rows E1-E4).
A starting holder of possession. PS1's initial value is a governed realization choice; this profile bounds the choice space and does not pick a team.
A static layout position for the ball, which the applicability entry on O4/O5 withdraws because a ball's location is game state.

defaultLaws.editionNote: He names no edition. The laws are cited by IFAB law number only, and nothing here depends on an edition's wording; the d26 design read Laws 1 and 12 from theifab.com, which showed the 2026/27 edition as current. Which edition governs is his to name.

words: The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.
We should not need to redefine ordinary soccer rules separately for every Learning Goal, game form, or activity.

Where a normal law cannot apply directly because of the modified field, scoring structure, or game format, the system should identify the relevant adaptation rather than silently assume conventional conditions exist.
The offside question, for example, may need an explicit ruling for this small-sided environment, but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws.
The governing principle is to inherit established sport rules and explicitly define only the necessary departures.

defaultLaws.restates: deliberatelyNotContributed[0], with his authority (item 10): no law is authored as an item or a line of the game; the Laws are named as the default, and the laws below are listed only because each can fail to apply in a modified environment. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R1): or, listed for DEPARTURE, only because an activity departs from it.
defaultLaws.note: Added 23 October 2026 (H2, the d26 design's build step 2, its section 3.2). A declaration, never items: his item 10 excludes reconstructing the laws as representation. Only the laws that can fail to apply in a modified environment and matter for the two build-out realizations are listed; every other law applies by default and is not listed. Each law's preconditions are written in the engine's closed, sport-neutral predicate vocabulary (back/src/system/derivation/default-laws.ts): applicableWhen says when the law can apply at all, requires what it needs to apply directly. The law ids, the names and the 'penalty-area' token are ours (DRAFT); the facts are cited by IFAB law number. An activity's provisional realization records its departures on its own items (departsFrom) and declares how strictly its activity is held (defaultLawsCheck); the account is computed after realization and shown to an administrator (back/src/system/realization/default-laws-check.ts). The five decisions of the note sent to him (the goal and the penalty area, the same-source pairing rule, offside, penalty kicks, the goal line, handling in the zone version) are his and are not filled here. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R1, the d27 design's section 2.6): each law says why it is listed (listedFor: ADAPTATION, a law that can fail to apply in a modified environment, which names the preconditions it needs; or DEPARTURE, a law listed only so an activity can record that it departs from it, which may need nothing to apply) and whether it is a law of how play restarts (restart, read by the account where a game holds the common dead-ball restart of register row RP1). Three laws are listed for DEPARTURE beside the six (LAW-8-DB, LAW-13, LAW-15), for his reply filed 27 October 2026, items 3 and 4 ("There should be no separate corners, goal kicks, throw-ins, free kicks, or penalty kicks for this activity."), so every restart his common restart replaces is departed from explicitly (his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10: "The governing principle is to inherit established sport rules and explicitly define only the necessary departures."). Penalty kicks and the ball over the goal line (decisions 3 and 4) are answered for the build-out activity by those items; offside (decision 2) is answered by his item 2 and is not carried here; the goal and its penalty area (decision 1) and handling in the zone version (his item 5) are not filled here. AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R3, the d27 design's stage R3, its section 2.6): offside is now carried, as a departure an activity's realization records on itself (a law it removes without replacing it, so no item carries it), never here; an activity's realization records its departures on its own items or, for such a law, on itself.

words: My preference is for standard soccer goalkeeper handling rules to apply, using a regulation penalty area whenever the playing environment can accommodate it appropriately.
The penalty area is an existing, meaningful part of the sport. We should avoid inventing a new handling region when an established one can serve the activity.
Use an existing regulation penalty area when the activity dimensions and setup permit it.
When a smaller field is necessary, use an explicitly defined and knowledge-authorized scaled penalty area.
I would not approve an undefined area that the coach simply points out, nor a feet-only goalkeeper restriction as the default for this realization.

Please investigate the smallest reusable method for representing an authorized penalty area, including its geometry and relationship to the goal and playing space. Do not assume a scaled dimension without knowledge support.
This should be a general soccer environment capability rather than a Goalkeeper Build-Out exception.

boundRegions.note: Added 23 October 2026 (H3, the d26 design's build step 3, its N3 and N5; register version 21). A declaration beside the profile's contribution, never items, like defaultLaws: which object kinds need a region bound to them (requirements), and the pairings authorized so far, each one named document giving an object, its region and its mark together - only that geometry comes with an entry (borrows), never the document's other provisions. That this table lives in the Sport Profile is OUR READING (the d26 design's N3): the profile admits constitutive sport structure when the selected game rules require it and no existing authoritative source supplies it (the ownership rule above), his item 10 selects the normal Laws, which key the goalkeeper's handling on a penalty area, and no knowledge source in the repository supplies one. BUILT WITH THE REGULATION ENTRY ONLY. A pairing is matched by the width the session states for its object, and nothing else: whether a smaller goal on a field wide enough for the regulation area takes that area or its own format's (the same-source pairing rule, decision 1b of the note sent to him) is his, so such a goal matches no entry and is a knowledge gap - never given the regulation area, never a scaled one. No scaled entry is recorded and no scaled size is assumed: a scaled entry is added only when he authorizes one named document (decision 1 of the note sent to him), with its values confirmed against that document's current edition. The goal type, height and format conditions are shown with the entry on the review page and are matched by nothing until a session can state them (the d26 design's build step 4). AMENDED 23 October 2026 (H4, register version 22): a session can now state its goals' type, from the register's closed list (full-size, scaled, mini-goal), so an entry is matched by the width AND the type the session states - an entry's type is one of that list's values - and where an entry of the stated width records a type the session does not state, the build asks for it, never assuming the entry's goal; a goal of another type is a knowledge gap, exactly as a goal of another width is. The height and the format conditions are still matched by nothing: no session is asked for a goal's height until an authorized entry reads it (his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 9(b)). Which goals suit a realization stays his decision 1. The requirement's id, the region noun and the 'penalty-area' token are ours (DRAFT). AMENDED 24 October 2026 (K1, the d27 design sections 1.1-1.7): the named FA 5v5 pairing is recorded, geometry only, as an initial field-test candidate (his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 1). Suitability now reads the stated type before width. Height and format conditions remain descriptive. The penalty mark is recorded but neither marked nor used (his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 3).

pairings.note: The regulation geometry, cited by IFAB law number (the d26 design read Laws 1 and 12 from theifab.com, which showed the 2026/27 edition as current; he names no edition, as in defaultLaws). Law 1.10: the goal is 7.32 m between the posts and 2.44 m to the crossbar. Law 1.6: the penalty area is set out 16.5 m from the inside of each goalpost, 16.5 m into the field of play, so 40.32 m wide with this goal; the penalty mark is 11 m from the midpoint between the goalposts. The type 'full-size' is the Goalkeeper Included Condition's own word ("Use full-size or scaled goals depending on field dimensions.", which he approved in his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 4). The mark is shown here; whether a spot is marked or paced, and whether penalty kicks apply at all, is decision 3 of the note sent to him, so no row records a spot. The players and age band are null: the Laws state neither as a condition on this geometry.

pairings.note: The goal is stated in feet (12ft x 6ft); widthM/heightM are the exact conversion at 0.3048 m per foot (ours; The FA's 2012 metric guide rounds to 3.66 x 1.83 m, not used). The depth is printed 9 m; The FA's 2012 metric guide gave 8 m and the 2025 edition 9 yd (8.2296 m) (1.3 (a)). The diagram does not name the rectangle or the dot; 'penalty area' and 'mark' are our reading from Laws 8, 12 and 14 of the same handbook. type 'scaled' is our reading of the Goalkeeper Included Condition's 'full-size or scaled goals'. Its other provisions (retreat line, pass or dribble-in, distances, heading law) do not come with it. Used at 40 x 30 m, larger than its pitch, chosen by space per player. The 9 m depth may be a misprint; we use 9 m as printed. his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 3: "The penalty-area specification may include a penalty spot, but this activity does not need to mark or use it."

items.value: the game's functional object is a ball

basisEvidence.quote: For this pilot scope it should establish only constitutive sport structure now demonstrated to be required: the game's functional object is a ball.

items.fitNote: EXISTS on a COLLECTION row establishes the element (SD-83 permits it; `establishesExistence` admits OWNER_RULING). valueStatus is N/A because EXISTS carries no value to range over (RC-6). The ball's count is deliberately unconstrained: no selected rule depends on how many there are, and GF2 and Wide Zone both declare the number of balls NON_CLAIMED. Its layout position is withdrawn by the applicability entry on O4/O5, so this item establishes a ball that exists and is nowhere in the static representation, which is the boundary applied rather than an omission.

items.value: one of the participating opposing teams the game establishes; the relationship holds between those teams and the ball of SPORT-SOCCER-01

basisEvidence.quote: Authorize a bounds-only contribution establishing the possession relationship as a legitimate game structure over the participating opposing teams, while leaving its initial holder as a governed realization choice unless more specific authoritative knowledge constrains it.

items.fitNote: BOUNDS-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND DELIBERATELY SO. `requirement: RANGE` is outside the entailing set {EQUALS, POSITIONED, ORIENTED}, and the value is a qualitative term rather than an array, so this contribution lands in `bounding` and never in `entailing` or `narrowing`. That is what makes PS1 an authorized choice rather than a resolved value: the representation establishes the relationship and its permitted participants, and realization chooses the initial holder. EXISTS could not be used — SD-100 makes EXISTS inert on a FIELD row. No team is named here; naming one would author game state the boundary excludes. The sport level says the relationship is valid and over whom; which team starts with the ball is not a fact about soccer.

declarations.note: doesNotConstrain: how many balls. No selected rule depends on the count, and two game forms already declare it unauthored.

doesNotConstrain: a ball's location is game state, not layout. The applicability entry on O4 withdraws the row for this kind; this declaration records that the silence is deliberate rather than unexamined.

SPORT-SOCCER-02 bounds the relationship over the participating opposing teams. The initial holder is left to realization under SD-39; the evolving holder is game state and is governed by POSSESSION_CHANGE rather than represented.
